note: Adversarial review findings (item-quality and compliance lenses), round 1, run on 18 Oct 2026 on the new device. Not yet acted on. Scratch evidence: ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-dev-10/ (probe10.py, probe10b.py, the probed *.grc graphs, probe10_results.json, probe10b_results.json, probe10c_results.json, rebuild/).

item-quality.verdict: Mostly sound; no blocking defect, but fix F1 (harness) and decide F2-F4 before acceptance. Confirmed: the instruction is self-contained and states every number the oracle uses (packet bytes and payload seed, MSB first, bit 0 -> +1, 5 samples per symbol, RRC 0.4, 1,056-symbol bursts and 4,000-sample gaps, 0.0005 cycles/sample, 0.0157 rad/symbol within 1 %). It names both observation points (symbols.dat complex, freq.dat float) and gives the symptom only: the quoted errors are exactly the four GRC reports (two IO-type, two IO-size), and GRC-Agent's inspect_graph reports validation status anyway, so they leak nothing extra. The start fails at V3 for the stated reason. Family repair / type_mismatch and level L2 are right (11 functional blocks, BPSK modulation and demodulation, a 5:1 rate change; the Correlation Estimator's tags are not consumed, so L3's 'tags' does not apply). Every valid alternative I wrote passes V6: M&M clock recovery after an RRC FIR; Symbol Sync (M&M TED, MMSE) after an RRC FIR; Symbol Sync (Gardner) with no matched filter (corr 0.978); the catalog-default init_phase 16 and max_dev 1.5; the Correlation Estimator removed (bursts move 62 symbols, inside the +-128 window); clock-sync loop_bw 0.01-0.2; Costas w 0.01-0.2. Wrong repairs are rejected. Real part -> fff -> complex fails V6 (corr 0.10-0.15, freq 0), as the fault note claims. Splitting I/Q into two fff clock syncs recovers the symbols (0.987) but fails the 1 % carrier check (+2.0 % / -1.95 %). The fault is easy, a single enum flip located by the quoted errors, but that is inherent to a type-mismatch repair; the item statistics will show whether it discriminates. Four findings survive: one medium (the ladder's tap stall misreports a natural wrong repair at V5) and three low.

findings.claim: A natural wrong repair fails at V5 (liveness) instead of V6. The funnel and Exec@1 therefore count it as a flowgraph that does not run. The repair: the model keeps the Float->Float clock sync and moves the Costas loop ahead of it (Correlation Estimator -> Costas -> Complex To Real -> clock sync fff -> Float To Complex -> symbols.dat; freq.dat stays on the Costas loop's second output). This graph validates, generates and runs, and its symbols are correct. It breaks only the stated 'radians per symbol' requirement: it holds 2*pi*0.0005 = 0.00314 rad/sample. The ladder taps every observation point with Head(8192). Here the freq tap runs at the sample rate, so it fills first and its Head finishes. From then on nothing reads the Costas loop's second output, and the Costas loop stalls. symbols.dat receives only 4,885 of the 8,192 items, so V5 fails on liveness. The verdict (fail) is right, but the rung is wrong. build.py's docstring already describes this stall when it explains the observation design, but nothing protects an answer that changes the rate of one tap.
findings.evidence: ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-dev-10/wrong_costas_first_fff.grc, run through ladder.check with task.json: first_failed V5, "liveness: an observation point received too few items {'symbols': 4885, 'freq': 8192}". The same graph with a copy of the task that observes only symbols.dat passes V5 (8,192 items) and every symbols check: bursts 0.9867/0.9867, preamble 0.9987, gap RMS 0.0. Its freq.dat holds 0.003142 in every gap, so V6 would have rejected it on the stated 0.0157 rad/symbol.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the tap in tier_f/_worker._run so that a full tap never blocks the graph. For example, drop Head, connect each tap straight to a vector sink, stop once every tap holds n_items, and truncate to n_items. Then re-run the gates of every task with more than one observation point. If the harness stays as it is, record in this item that an answer whose two observation points run at different rates fails at V5, and treat this item's rung diagnostics accordingly in the Exec@1 analysis.

findings.claim: The instruction states structural requirements that V6 does not check. freq.dat must hold 'the Costas loop's frequency estimate (its second output)', and symbols.dat must hold the 'recovered symbols' of the receive chain ('Keep the packet, the modulation, the burst timing, the channel ...'). oracle.graph_checks is absent, so an answer that writes the expected numbers without receiving anything passes. Under the 16 Oct oracle policy, structural wording needs a graph check (or behavioural rewording). In the one-edit repair setting such a shortcut is unlikely, hence low.
findings.evidence: shortcut_synthesised_outputs.grc passes V1-V6 (corr 1.0/1.0, preamble 1.0, freq 0.015708, gap RMS 0). In it the clock sync and the Costas loop are deleted and the Correlation Estimator is parked on a Null Sink. A repeating Vector Source of the 1,056 packet symbols plus 800 zeros feeds symbols.dat through a Throttle, and a Constant Source 0.015708 feeds freq.dat. shortcut_freq_constant.grc also passes V6: it has the correct ccf fix, but freq.dat is fed by a Constant Source 2*pi*0.0005*5 and the Costas loop's second output is parked. I also tried two candidate graph checks: block_present digital_costas_loop_cc, and path channels_channel_model -> blocks_file_sink via digital_costas_loop_cc. They accept the reference, the 3 variants and the 21 other valid graphs I probed, and they reject the full synthesis. They cannot reject the freq-constant shortcut, because graph_checks has no port- or sink-specific edge check.
findings.suggested_fix: Add oracle.graph_checks (group main): {kind: block_present, ids: [digital_costas_loop_cc]} and {kind: path, from_ids: [channels_channel_model], to_ids: [blocks_file_sink], via_ids: [digital_costas_loop_cc]}. For the source of freq.dat, choose one: (a) extend graph_checks with an edge check (from_ids plus from_port -> to_ids plus to_params such as {file: freq.dat}) and require digital_costas_loop_cc port 1 -> the freq.dat File Sink; or (b) accept the gap and record it.

findings.claim: The f2p carrier checks average freq.dat over the gaps. There the Costas loop holds the value it was left with after the burst's truncated trailing edge, not its steady-state estimate. That value depends on the loop bandwidth w, which the instruction leaves free, and lands anywhere from -0.47 % to +1.03 % off the stated value. The stated 1 % therefore has no margin. A correct receiver with w = 0.25 is rejected although its symbols are perfect and its in-burst estimate is exact; w = 0.3 passes by less than 0.001 %. The run is deterministic, so this is a problem of where the value is measured, not flakiness. A repair model is unlikely to touch w, hence low.
findings.evidence: probe10b.py, probe10b_results.json and probe10c_results.json: the reference with only the Costas w changed. Gap value by w: 0.01 -> 0.015708, 0.03 -> 0.015713, 0.0628 (reference) -> 0.015728, 0.1 -> 0.015754, 0.126 -> 0.015777, 0.15 -> 0.015800, 0.2 -> 0.015844, 0.25 -> 0.015869 (+1.03 %, V6 FAIL on both carrier checks), 0.3 -> 0.015865 (+0.999 %), 0.4 -> 0.015779, 0.5 -> 0.015634 (-0.47 %). The mean over symbols 300-800 of burst 1 is 0.015707-0.015729 for every w. Clock-sync loop_bw 0.01-0.2 moves the gap value only within 0.015726-0.015729. The I/Q-split kludge gives +2.0 % and -1.95 % in the two checked gaps (-2.3 % and +2.1 % in the unchecked first and last gaps). Every carrier mutant is far outside 2 %: no offset, twice the offset, w = 0.0005 never converges, phase output, and sps 4 at -20 %.
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) state and check 'within 1.5 %': every probed w from 0.01 to 0.5 falls within the range -0.47 % to +1.03 %, and the I/Q kludge and every carrier mutant are still rejected. Or (b) measure the estimate while a burst is being received (e.g. symbols 300-800 of bursts 1 and 2, where every w is within 0.14 %) and reword the instruction to 'while a burst is being received, once the loop has locked'. Option (b) may let the I/Q-split kludge pass (not probed), which is acceptable by behaviour. The team decides; then re-run the gates.

findings.claim: The instruction says the Stream Mux 'sends one packet (1,056 symbols = 5,280 samples) and then 4,000 zero samples', and it requires 'every burst reproducing the transmitted preamble and payload symbols'. But the Constellation Modulator's RRC filter delays the symbol stream by 27 symbols (135 samples; the filter spans 55 symbols). Each 5,280-sample burst therefore carries the last 27 symbols of the previous packet followed by the first 1,029 symbols of its own packet; the first burst instead starts with a 27-symbol filter ramp. So even the reference does not reproduce a whole packet in each burst. Its per-burst packet correlation is sqrt(1029/1056) = 0.987, and the check passes only because the threshold is 0.9, which the instruction does not state. The receiver does reproduce the transmitted stream exactly. No correct repair fails because of this, but the description is wrong, and the thresholds behind 'reproducing' (corr >= 0.9) and 'silence' (RMS <= 0.05) are not stated.
findings.evidence: Reference capture (probe10.py, runs/): bursts start at symbols 93, 1922, 3778, 5634 and 7490. For bursts 1-3, the packet aligns best 27 symbols after the burst starts (shift 27, corr 0.98727); for burst 0 it aligns at the start. The first 27 symbols of burst 1 equal the last 27 packet symbols (27/27 match). Hard decisions over the 1,029 packet symbols of burst 1 give 0 errors. sqrt(1029/1056) = 0.98714 matches the reported 0.987.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the stream rather than whole packets. For example: 'The Stream Mux alternates 5,280 samples of the modulator's output with 4,000 zero samples; because of the modulator's pulse-shaping delay, each burst starts with the last 27 symbols of the previous packet.' And: 'the recovered symbols must reproduce the transmitted symbol stream (up to a constant phase rotation and a fixed delay), with silence between the bursts.' In the oracle notes, record that 0.987 is the ceiling and that the 0.9 threshold allows for the 27-symbol shift.

compliance.verdict: Compliant; one low finding. I re-ran ./gb tier-f gates items/tier_f/dev/gbf-dev-10 on 18 Oct (exit 0). Solvability 10/10 at 8 workers; size 1,181 tokens (limit 3,000); 3/3 variants pass V6; the start fails at V3, as fault.expected_rung says; 13/13 mutants reach V5 and all are killed. The new gates.json has the same content as the previous one. Split: the seed digital/demod/test_corr_est.grc is 'dev' in splits/flowgraph_seed_split.json, and its sha256 (5fe522f4...) matches both the split file and /usr/share/gnuradio/examples. The task is seed-derived, so signature shopping does not apply. The licence GPL-3.0-or-later matches the split record. The source, cluster_id, provenance (drafted_by Claude (Anthropic)) and review (pending-team-review) fields are present and correct, and id, directory and split agree. I checked all nine perturbation entries against the original example and all are right: samp_rate 100000, sps 4, eb 0.35, preamble ac dd ..., payload 992, the random.getrandbits payload, gap 20000, freq_offset a Qt range at 0, mark_delay 1. noise (0) and time_offset (1) are unchanged and correctly not listed. Every mutation breaks a stated requirement and reaches V5. Tolerances: the 1 % is stated; corr >= 0.9 and gap RMS <= 0.05 are lenient stand-ins for 'reproducing' and 'silence' (item-quality F3, F4). The canary GUID appears only in task.json; it is not in the instruction, start.grc, reference.grc or the variants. Disjointness holds. No training-side spec uses this seed, a Polyphase Clock Sync or a Costas loop: t05_qam_debug's demo_qam.grc is a channels/impairments demo with no synchroniser, and t25 is knowledge-only. The 17 Oct Tier-F dev contamination report has no flags for this item (n-gram coverage 0, max embedding similarity 0.83). build.py regenerates task.json, reference.grc, start.grc and all three variants byte-identically (rebuilt in ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-dev-10/rebuild; cmp identical).

findings.claim: gbf-test-17 (test split, repair, L2, seed digital/demod/pam_timing.grc) faults the same block: a Polyphase Clock Sync whose validation fails at V3. There the cause is an undefined variable spb in sps and taps; the receiver is a PSK timing-recovery receiver from the same example directory. By eval plan §6 the two are not twins: source file, fault type, modulation and oracle all differ, and the source-file split rule is met. Still, choices made on dev with this item (prompt, checkpoint) train on the same 'fix the Polyphase Clock Sync's parameters' skill that test-17 measures.
findings.evidence: items/tier_f/test/gbf-test-17/task.json: fault {type: undefined_variable, variable: spb, expected_rung: V3}; its instruction says '... validation reports that two parameters of the Polyphase Clock Sync block (Samples/Symbol and Taps) cannot be evaluated'. Both cluster_ids are under digital/demod/. No other first-set task uses digital_pfb_clock_sync_xxx, digital_costas_loop_cc or digital_corr_est_cc.
findings.suggested_fix: No change required. Record the relation (e.g. a related-items note) so the set-level critic and the team see it. If the team wants different faulted blocks across dev and test, move this item's fault to another part of the chain (team decision).
